newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai finmin seeks 59 bln baht govt spending cuts.
newsitem.headline: Thai finmin seeks 59 bln baht govt spending cuts.

text.p: Thai Finance Minister Amnuay Viravan said on Tuesday he would seek cabinet approval of a proposed six percent cut in government spending to help him balance budget for the fiscal year ending September 30, 1997.
Amnuay told reporters the planned 59 billion baht ($2.27 billion) budget cut would include over 40 billion baht spending on infrastructure projects proposed by state enterprises.

Amnuay's announcement followed a government estimate last week that Thailand's slowing economy would reduce government revenue to about 925 billion baht in the current fiscal year from 984 billion projected earlier.
He said the planned budget cut, designed also to help Thailand curb its current account deficit, would also include about 15 billion baht in normal operating expenditure of government agencies.
The minister said infrastructure projects affected by the cut are new low priority utilities which could be delayed and those with high import content.
The Bank of Thailand has projected that the Thai current account deficit would narrow to 7.9 percent of gross domestic product in 1997 from 8.2 percent in 1996.
